correctness.rationale: Testing invariance with antiderivatives in V gives \(\mathbb E[g_K(V-V_K)W\mid V]=F(V)\), including at \(V=V_K\) without division. Testing in W and normalizing by \(q(V)>0\) gives \(\mathbb E_\nu[W_\infty(V)\mid W]=W\). Orthogonal conditional-variance decompositions yield exactly the two displayed speed defects. Zero voltage defect makes V constant, after which bounded completeness forces the scalar gate equation to its equilibrium; zero gate defect and strict monotonicity of \(W_\infty\) force both coordinates constant. Nonzero zero-mean coordinate speeds therefore cross both signs. The exact checker verifies the abstract regression variance identity and the rate-tilt algebra.

final_claim: For the standard autonomous two-dimensional Morris--Lecar system with \(C,g_K>0\), positive gate rate \(q(V)\), and strictly increasing \(W_\infty\), every compact invariant probability measure satisfies the voltage-fiber current regression under \(\mu\) and the gate-nullcline regression under the \(q\)-tilted measure \(\nu\), with the two exact variance--speed defects, equilibrium rigidity, and two-sided nullcline crossing stated in RESULT.md.
limitations: Compactly supported invariant measures and constant applied current only.
The gate regression is under the rate-tilted measure \(d\nu\propto q(V)d\mu\), not generally under the physical stationary law.
No period, firing-rate, bifurcation, or full-density formula.
